question.text: If a USDINR 84 call option has premium Rs. 0.50 and delta of 0.70, and USDINR rises by Re 1 to 85, the approximate new premium is:

explanation.text: The Logic: Delta is the change in option premium per unit change in the underlying. Approximate premium change = Delta x Underlying change = 0.70 x 1.00 = Rs. 0.70. New premium is approximately 0.50 + 0.70 = Rs. 1.20. The Trap: Delta itself can change as the underlying moves; the linear delta approximation is therefore only an estimate, not an exact new premium. Note: Page 73 of the NISM Series-I workbook defines delta as the change in option premium per unit change in the underlying and gives this calculation method. Pages 74 and 77 support gamma as a delta-change measure and option-pricing output.
